Online education platform for legitimate internet income
Kenya — ages 18–30, expandable to broader East Africa

Biza is a structured, mobile-first learning platform that teaches young Kenyans exactly how every legitimate online income model works — including the process, requirements, realistic timelines, startup costs, platforms, and scam red flags. It addresses a critical gap in the Kenyan digital economy: widespread misinformation and fraud around online income opportunities.
Note on domain: biza.co.ke, biza.io, biza.app, and biza.com are all taken by unrelated businesses. The product brand remains "Biza" — accessed via getbiza.co.ke.
Millions of young Kenyans seek online income but encounter misinformation, scams, and unstructured information.
Existing YouTube content is fragmented, often monetised through hype, and rarely Kenya-specific.
No single trusted platform explains how online money actually works end-to-end.
Users waste time and money on fraudulent schemes that a proper foundation would prevent.
There is no platform that builds fraud awareness and honest expectations before teaching methods.

Biza provides verified, structured learning paths for every major legitimate online income category. Each course follows a flexible chapter-based framework — content depth drives structure, not a fixed template. Every opportunity page shows honest data: startup cost in KES, realistic timeline, success rate, risk levels, and required skills. The onboarding flow includes a dedicated mindset and fraud awareness phase — making Biza the only Kenyan edtech platform that prepares users to recognise scams before teaching them to earn.
Every tier is a database record — nothing is hardcoded in the frontend. Adding a new category, opportunity, or course requires only a database entry, not a code change.

While other platforms teach how to earn, Biza also teaches what to avoid and why, with specific, documented fraud patterns relevant to young Kenyans.

24.5 Anti-scam alert — opportunity info card component
Every opportunity info card includes a scam-specific alert below the risk section. Examples:
Dropshipping: "Legitimate dropshipping suppliers never charge you before you make a sale. If a supplier asks for upfront membership fees — walk away."
Affiliate marketing: "Legitimate affiliate programmes are free to join. Any programme charging an entry fee to become an affiliate is a scam."
Forex / trading: "No signal group, coach, or bot can guarantee trading profits. If someone promises consistent returns — it is fraud."
Freelancing: "No legitimate client asks you to pay a registration or verification fee to receive work. Real clients pay you."
